about.title: Hello, I'm *Elena*.
about.p1: I grew up in Slovakia and have lived in Vienna for many years. I studied philosophy and the arts, raised three children, and walked pilgrim roads from Tamil Nadu to Assisi.
about.p2: Along the way I learned something simple to say and hard to live: a whole life is not one where you carry more, but one where you *choose* what to carry. This is what I help women do.

way.title: Four clearings to make *room* for your life
way.intro:
Decluttering is not only about drawers and calendars. It is about deciding, gently and honestly,
what still deserves a place in your life. We work through four clearings, at your pace.

items.name: Space
items.question: What surrounds me?
items.line: Your home and the things you live with every day.

items.name: Time
items.question: What receives my life?
items.line: Where your days, energy and attention really go.

items.name: Relationships
items.question: Who and what has access to me?
items.line: The people, roles and expectations you carry.

items.name: Inner life
items.question: What am I devoted to?
items.line: The values and longings beneath it all.

items.name: 1:1 Coaching
items.line: We work through the four clearings together, one by one, at your own pace.

items.name: Women's circle
items.line: Six to eight women meeting over a few months, clearing space together.

items.name: La Via del Cuore
items.line: A walking pilgrimage from Assisi to Spoleto for women in transition.

items.quote: I had the job, the flat in Vienna, the 'perfect' life, and felt nothing. With Elena I finally asked myself what I want. Today I'm living it.
items.name: Katarína

items.quote: After my divorce I didn't know who I was anymore. Elena helped me come back to myself, gently and honestly.
items.name: Sophie

items.quote: Clarity first, then courage, then action. I stopped waiting for permission to change my life.

meta.title: My journey · Aurea
meta.description: Philosophy, heritage, gender studies, Indian classical dance, Vedānta, contemplative prayer, pilgrimage and motherhood: the journey of Elena Repka.

journeyPage.title: A life of crossing *boundaries*
journeyPage.intro: My life has been a long inquiry into how we create meaning through body, culture, place and ritual. These are the places it has taken me.
journeyPage.closing: Not a collection of places, but one question: how to live a *whole* life.

places.line: Where it began: philosophy, art and European aesthetics.
Among the Minangkabau, where house, land and lineage pass through women.
Classical dance, Vedānta and the sacred sites of the South.
The Char Dham Yatra, high in the mountains.
On the way of Mary Magdalene.
In the footsteps of St Francis and St Clare.
Weeks of silence and prayer with Benedictine monks.
Today: research, coaching, and three grown children.

pilgrimagePage.title:
Not escaping life.
*Walking back* into it.
pilgrimagePage.intro: A walking pilgrimage for women in transition, from Assisi to Spoleto through the green heart of Umbria.
is: A threshold for women in a season of change
Simple meals, simple rooms, a small group of women
Time to reconsider what you carry
pilgrimagePage.routeIntro: We walk in the footsteps of St Francis and St Clare, from one Umbrian town to the next.
pilgrimagePage.road: You leave your ordinary life behind. You carry less. You walk, and you get tired. You sleep somewhere different and eat simply. You talk, and you become quiet. You meet other women. And slowly, you reconsider what you carry.
pilgrimagePage.returnText: The pilgrimage does not end in Spoleto. Together we prepare the way back, so that what you found on the road has a place in your everyday life. The question is not only what you leave behind, but what you *carry home*.

meta.description: Women on the threshold: embodied pilgrimage, Marian devotion and the reorganisation of women's lives. Research by Elena Repka.

researchPage.title: Women on the *threshold*
researchPage.subtitle: Embodied pilgrimage, Marian devotion and the reorganisation of women's lives
researchPage.intro: My research grows out of my own life: years of walking, praying and studying sacred traditions across Europe and India. It asks what pilgrimage does to women, and what women do with pilgrimage when they return home.
questions: How do women negotiate the boundary between traditional Catholic devotion and contemporary forms of spirituality?
What happens to the meaning of pilgrimage after returning home?
What does a woman carry home, and what does she leave behind?
researchPage.field: Ethnographic research among women pilgrims to Mariazell, Austria's most important Marian shrine, and among the ageing communities along its pilgrim paths.
researchPage.comparative: A dialogue between two traditions of embodied transformation: European Christian pilgrimage, with its walking, sacred landscapes and return, and Indian embodied traditions, with their attention to body, consciousness, ritual and Śakti.
researchPage.positionality: As both researcher and pilgrim, I make my own position transparent: this is reflexive ethnography, written from inside the experience it studies.
researchPage.contactText: For conferences, academic exchange and research collaboration, I'd be glad to hear from you.
